title: Μάντις
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 233 (= Perry 161). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Μάντις ἐπὶ τῆς ἀγορᾶς καθεζόμενος ἠργυρολόγει.
sentences.tr: Mantis epi tēs agoras kathezomenos ērgyrologei.
sentences.l: A seer, seated in the market-place, was collecting money.
sentences.n: A μάντις read signs — birds, entrails, dreams — for a fee, and the market-place was where he set up. The imperfect ἠργυρολόγει gives the trade he plied, not a single day's takings.

sentences.t: Ἐλθόντος δέ τινος αἰφνίδιον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπαγγείλαντος ὡς τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ αἱ θύραι ἀνεσπασμέναι εἰσὶ καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔνδον ἐκπεφορημένα, ἐκταραχθεὶς ἀνεπήδησε καὶ στενάξας ᾔει δρόμῳ τὸ γεγονὸς ὀψόμενος.
sentences.tr: Elthontos de tinos aiphnidion pros auton kai apangeilantos hōs tēs oikias autou hai thyrai anespasmenai eisi kai panta ta endon ekpephorēmena, ektarachtheis anepēdēse kai stenaxas ēiei dromōi to gegonos opsomenos.
sentences.l: But someone having come to him suddenly and announced that the doors of his house have been wrenched off and everything inside carried out, he, thrown into confusion, leapt up and, groaning, went at a run to see what had happened.
sentences.i: But when a man came up to him suddenly with the news that the doors of his house had been wrenched off and everything inside carried away, he was thrown into confusion, sprang up, and with a groan went off at a run to see what had happened.
sentences.n: One genitive absolute carries two participles, ἐλθόντος and ἀπαγγείλαντος, over a single subject τινος. After ὡς the messenger's own tenses are kept — perfect ἀνεσπασμέναι εἰσί, 'have been wrenched off' — where English moves them back. ὀψόμενος is a future participle of purpose, the regular way of saying 'in order to see'; ᾔει is the imperfect of εἶμι, 'was on his way'.

sentences.t: Τῶν δὲ παρατυχόντων τις θεασάμενος εἶπεν· « Ὦ οὗτος, σὺ τὰ ἀλλότρια πράγματα προειδέναι ἐπαγγελλόμενος τὰ σαυτοῦ οὐ προεμαντεύου ; »
sentences.tr: Tōn de paratychontōn tis theasamenos eipen· « Ō houtos, sy ta allotria pragmata proeidenai epangellomenos ta sautou ou proemanteuou ; »
sentences.l: And one of those who happened to be present, having seen it, said: « You there, you who profess to foreknow other people's affairs, were you not prophesying your own? »
sentences.i: One of the bystanders saw it and said: « You there — you who advertise that you can foresee other men's business, were you not prophesying your own? »
sentences.n: Ὦ οὗτος is a blunt hail across a crowd, roughly 'hey, you'. ἐπαγγέλλομαι in the middle is to announce oneself as able to do a thing, the word for a professional's advertised claim.

sentences.t: Τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ χρήσαιτο ἄν τις πρὸς ἐκείνους τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς τὸν ἑαυτῶν βίον φαύλως διοικοῦντας καὶ τῶν μηδὲν προσηκόντων προνοεῖσθαι πειρωμένους.
sentences.tr: Toutōi tōi logōi chrēsaito an tis pros ekeinous tous anthrōpous tous ton heautōn bion phaulōs dioikountas kai tōn mēden prosēkontōn pronoeisthai peirōmenous.
sentences.l: This story someone might use against those men who manage their own life badly and attempt to take forethought for the things that in no way belong to them.
sentences.i: One might use this story against people who manage their own life badly and set about providing for matters that are no concern of theirs.
sentences.n: προνοέομαι takes the genitive of what one provides for, hence τῶν μηδὲν προσηκόντων, 'the things pertaining in no way'. διοικέω is the word for running a household or a city — administration, not chance.
